Steadier RAM in the guided renderer, portamento that glides like BASSMIDI, and a heads-up when a new version is out.

## Downloads

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `kestrel-1.1.1-windows-x64.zip` | Windows 10/11 |
| `kestrel-1.1.1-macos-universal.dmg` | macOS 11 or newer (Apple silicon and Intel) |
| `kestrel-1.1.1-linux-x64.tar.gz` | Linux (Ubuntu 22.04 or newer) |

- **Windows:** unzip and double-click `kestrel.exe`. If SmartScreen warns you, click **More info → Run anyway**.
- **macOS:** copy `kestrel` out of the dmg. The first time you open it, allow it under **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**.
- **Linux:** extract it and run `./kestrel` in a terminal. You need a Vulkan driver.

The macOS and Linux builds haven't been tested yet. If you try one, please [open an issue](https://github.com/thtstickyboi/kestrel-midi/issues) and tell us how it went.

## What's new

- **Portamento.** CC5, CC65 and CC84 now glide the way BASSMIDI plays them.
- **Update notices.** The guided renderer tells you when a newer Kestrel is out. It never downloads anything. Choose the Fast Ring (every release) or the Slow Ring (feature releases only) in Extras, or set `KESTREL_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` to turn it off.
- **Remembered folders.** The MIDI, soundfont and destination pickers open where you left off, even after a restart. Kestrel keeps them in `ktrl.ini` next to the executable.
- **An API command for GUIs.** `check_update` lets a GUI show the same notice. See [API.md](https://github.com/thtstickyboi/kestrel-midi/blob/main/API.md).

## Fixes

- **The guided renderer no longer holds your soundfont in RAM twice.** Typing a flag such as `--volume` at the last step kept the first copy while the render loaded a second. With a large piano library, the peak went from about 2 GB back down to 1.1 GB.
